sections_read: Results: WP-PP, RP-BP, MP, AF incl. performance tests and movement duration
Discussion: summary of main results, quality of evidence, potential biases, agreements with other studies

entries.design: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of 15 RCTs (695 participants); Cochrane risk-of-bias tool
entries.population: Medical and physiotherapy students and residents; mostly surgical procedures (orthopaedic bone plating, laparoscopy, gynaecology, colonoscopy, joint mobilisation)
entries.intervention: whole vs part practice; random vs blocked practice; mental practice (added or substituted); terminal vs concurrent augmented feedback
entries.comparator: the respective alternative schedule or no additional practice

outcome.measure: procedure-specific checklists, global rating scales, error scores, movement duration
outcome.delay: mostly immediate post-acquisition (0-10 min); some delayed retention 5 days to 6 weeks; few transfer tests (e.g. cadaver instead of artificial bone)
outcome.transfer: near; one study each for most transfer tests

estimate.value: mental practice post-acquisition SMD 0.43 [0.01, 0.85] (241 participants), transfer 0.20 [-0.56, 0.97]; random vs blocked post-acquisition 0.63 [-0.10, 1.36] (n = 31, 2 studies), transfer -0.22 [-1.36, 0.92] favouring blocked (1 study); feedback: delayed retention -0.35 [-0.78, 0.08] favouring concurrent, transfer 0.94 [0.18, 1.70] favouring terminal (1 study, n = 30)
estimate.note: Several values extracted by the authors from graphs; most comparisons rest on 1-5 small studies.

entries.bias_and_applicability: All included studies rated high risk of bias (no blinding of learners/educators; sequence generation poorly reported; detection bias unclear in three). Almost all tests immediately after practice, which the authors state gives only limited evidence of learning. In the random-vs-blocked studies the benefit reversed on a more complex transfer task (cadaver bone), consistent with task-complexity moderation. Simulation and real procedures were pooled for mental practice.
